Quality review found no release-blocking defect in f9b43088..86c4b2d.

  • Governing instructions: Reviewed root, Python and Rust AGENTS.md, source ownership, testing and contribution rules.
  • Test quality — minor P3: The new tests at tests/autodiff/test_periodic_dispatch_methods.py:159–163, :197–201 and tests/autodiff/test_torch.py:259–265 use handwritten central differences. The testing guide explicitly requires treams_rs.testing.check_gradient for scalar objectives. These are meaningful regression tests, but replacing their finite-difference plumbing with that helper would follow the established standard without changing their cases or tolerances.
  • Resource note: The new diffraction-order allocation test grows a vector under an 8 GiB address-space limit and may consume several GiB before the expected refusal. Avoid rerunning it locally on limited hardware; the supplied current-head hosted CI already passed it.
  • No other findings: The shared lattice normalization addresses actual supported input forms; coordinate guards prevent silent truncation; mixed Torch constants preserve precision and gradients. Generated API pages match the generator and docstring edits. The changelog, citation metadata, release checks and documented limitations agree.

Read-only source review only. I ran no tests, builds or linters and changed no files or external state.
